results.content: # Exhibitions in Vienna. The city has numerous history, science, and art exhibitions on (or planned) at any one time. * Collecting for the Future at the Albertina (until October 11th): 250 years of the collection illustrated by masterpieces that include the rarely-seen *Young Hare* by Albrecht Dürer. * Canaletto & Bellotto at the Kunsthistorisches Museum (until September 6th, 2026): 18th-century cityscapes of Venice, London, Dresden, and Vienna. * Collecting for the Future: celebrating 250 years of the Albertina with an exhibition that explores the origins of the collection and how many of the great works became part of it. * Women Artists of the Albertina: highlights works by women artists in the collection, dating back as far as the 1400s (October 30th, 2026 to February 14th, 2027). * Common Story: a look at the history (which dates back to 1861) and future of the Künstlerhaus artist association, particularly its exhibitions and associated themes as shown in posters (July 3rd to September 27th, 2026).

Discover the captivating exhibitions at the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna – masterpieces, special exhibitions and highlights from the history of art! ## Our permanent exhibitions in the Neue Hofburg. ## Special exhibitions. We regularly hold special exhibitions to showcase our large collection. ## Our permanent exhibitions. Access via the Weltmuseum Wien with the admission ticket for the Weltmuseum Wien, Court Hunting and Armory Chamber and Collection of Ancient Musical Instruments. A central sculpture of seated figures is displayed at the bottom of the stairs, surrounded by intricately decorated columns and large windows that allow natural light to illuminate the space. Marvel at the enchanting treasures of the Kunstkammer, uncover ancient secrets in the Egyptian and Near Eastern Collection, and journey into the mythical realms of gods and heroes in the Collection of Greek and Roman Antiquities. Marvel at the legendary treasure of the Order of the Golden Fleece and come face to face with mythic wonders like the agate bowl once believed to be the Holy Grail and the world’s largest cut emerald.
